_purpose: Hand-authored, USER-APPROVED per-entity lede + short 'why this number' copy (Charter R4 prose home). NEVER auto-derived: a lede must accurately summarize the Wallach corpus and a why must accurately explain how the target was reached, so each is written one at a time and approved by Luneth. An entity absent here shows NO lede / NO why (never a guessed one). Read via state/entity-copy.ts; on the clean surface (_CLEAN_SURFACE_STORES) with lede/why as prose homes. conditions{} fills in as condition pages land (H2 chunk 2).

calcium.lede: The most abundant mineral in your body — about 1 kg of you, 99% locked in bone and teeth, the last 1% running your muscles, nerves and heartbeat.
calcium.why: From Wallach's Epigenetics (2014) dose table: 600–1,000 mg per 100 lb of body weight, scaled to a 154 lb adult ≈ 1,500 mg/day.

selenium.lede: The body's most efficient antioxidant — a trace mineral needed in only micrograms, yet the one Wallach ties to cystic fibrosis, Keshan heart failure, and much of cancer.
selenium.why: From Wallach's Epigenetics (2014) mineral table: 100–200 mcg per 100 lb of body weight; taking the upper figure scaled to a 154 lb adult ≈ 310 mcg/day.

copper.lede: A cofactor for hundreds of enzymes — it colours your hair and gives artery walls their elasticity, which is why Wallach reads premature grey as the first sign of a shortage.
copper.why: From Wallach's Epigenetics (2014) mineral table: 1–2 mg per 100 lb of body weight; taking the upper figure scaled to a 154 lb adult ≈ 3.1 mg/day.

zinc.lede: A trace mineral the body holds barely two grams of — and one of the few that is never burned for energy, but built into the tools your cells work with.
zinc.why: From Wallach's Epigenetics (2014) mineral table: 15–30 mg per 100 lb of body weight; taking the upper figure scaled to a 154 lb adult ≈ 46 mg/day.

magnesium.lede: The mineral at the centre of chlorophyll — what makes plants green and stores the sun's energy — and, inside you, calcium's counterweight: the "relaxer" that lets every muscle and nerve stand down.
magnesium.why: From Wallach's Epigenetics (2014) mineral table: 250–500 mg per 100 lb of body weight; taking the upper figure scaled to a 154 lb adult ≈ 770 mg/day.

vitamin-a.lede: The vitamin your eyes need to see in dim light — and, beyond vision, the one Wallach ties to healthy skin and mucous membranes, to bone and teeth, and to a lower risk of epithelial cancers.
vitamin-a.why: From Wallach's Epigenetics (2014): retinol 2,500–5,000 IU and β-carotene 5,000–25,000 IU. Taking the upper figure of each and converting at 0.3 mcg RAE per IU ≈ 1,500 mcg retinol + 7,500 mcg β-carotene = 9,000 mcg RAE/day.

chocolate.lede: Wallach reads a craving for chocolate as a mineral-shortage signal, not a sweet tooth — and rates bitter, low-glycemic dark cocoa, rich in brain-active compounds, well above sugary milk chocolate.

resveratrol.lede: The red-wine antioxidant behind the 'French Paradox' and the old 'Grape Cure' — Wallach says it flips on the same anti-aging switch (the sirtuins) as a calorie-restricted diet, and studies show it stretching animal lifespans.

hunza.lede: The remote Himalayan people Wallach holds up as living proof of his thesis: for 2,300 years they drank mineral-rich glacial 'milk' and grew food in wood-ash-fed soil — and routinely lived past 80, many past 100, nearly free of chronic disease.

longevity.lede: Wallach's account of why some reach 100 in good health and others don't: not genes but minerals, a calorie-restricted diet, antioxidants, and avoiding the modern 'land mines' — the same levers he finds in every long-lived culture.

centenarian-cultures.lede: The world's longest-lived peoples — Hunza, Vilcabamba, Okinawa, the Blue Zones — and the one thing Wallach says they share: not good genes, but a daily flood of 60-plus minerals from glacial water, culinary ashes and mineral-rich soil.

colloidal_minerals.lede: Plant-derived minerals ground so fine they stay suspended in liquid — the form Wallach says the body actually absorbs. It's why he points to glacial 'milk' and plant sources over rock and metal, and calls them the supplement to start with.

minerals.lede: The elements Wallach calls the currency of life: of the 75 metals on the periodic table, at least 60 have a job in the human body, and running short on them is where he traces most disease back to.
